document.abstract: This paper is a case history of the manufacture and distribution of 35-mm motion picture projection and sound equipment under wartime restrictions as imposed by War Production Board regulations. It tells about the difficulties and problems which were encountered and overcome so that the Armed Forces might obtain all of the equipment needed, with a limited quantity for our civilian theaters. The paper also discusses the reasons why our manufacturers cannot now produce as much new equipment as will be needed for replacements, and makes recommendations for future planning.
